item.title: [ecmascript] Terminology on the page explaining the function* declaration
item.content:encoded:
MDN URL

https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Statements/function*

What specific section or headline is this issue about?

Description, rest of the page

What information was incorrect, unhelpful, or incomplete?

In this page about the function* declaration, the subject terminology is setup early in the description, using the terms “GeneratorFunction” and “Generator”.

A function* declaration creates a
GeneratorFunction
object. Each time a generator function is called, it returns a new
Generator object […]

After this, throughout the page, the term “Generator” is used consistently to refer to the function* construct, i.e., the “GeneratorFunction”, not the result of a call to the “GeneratorFunction”.

This quite confused me.

What did you expect to see?

A consistent terminology in a page describing a quite complex subject in the first place.

Do you have any supporting links, references, or citations?

No response

Do you have anything more you want to share?

No response

item.title: [ecmascript] Yielding rejected promises from a sync generator now properly closes the iterator
item.content:encoded:
MDN URL

https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Statements/for-await...of

What specific section or headline is this issue about?

From Note: until but not including Specification.

What information was incorrect, unhelpful, or incomplete?

It seems at least modern Chrome does correctly call finally in the specified circumstances.

Assuming this is the case in all modern browsers and is perhaps even specified as such,
the corresponding content should be removed.

What did you expect to see?

No warning about an obsolete issue, assuming it actually is.

Do you have any supporting links, references, or citations?

Someone should check what the relevant spec says, I'm too busy, sorry.
